summary: Halyard template mutual NDA with VectraFlow edits adding a non-compete, deleting the independent development carve-out, narrowing the evidence standard, adding a 50,000 pound fixed payment, widening Representatives and extending return time to 15 Business Days.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party undertakes to the Disclosing Party that it shall:
findings.why: Disclosing Party and Receiving Party are defined by role so obligations bind both Parties equally.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: Definition is limited to information disclosed for the Purpose, covers marked or reasonably confidential information and derived notes and analyses, and protects both Parties.

findings.quote: a potential commercial [[DEL: relationship]] [[INS: partnership and software integration]] between them (the Purpose)
findings.why: The Purpose is widened from a commercial relationship to a partnership and software integration, which is still a defined discussion purpose and not use for any purpose, with use restricted to the Purpose in clause 2.1.2.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: and not during the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months thereafter develop, market or license any software product that competes directly with the core functionality of the Disclosing Party's software products as disclosed under this Agreement
findings.why: The inserted wording is a non-compete restricting development, marketing or licensing of competing software for the term plus 12 months.
findings.draft_redline: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to accept a non-compete in an NDA; the use restriction to the Purpose and the confidentiality obligations already protect each party's disclosed information. We have restored the original wording.

findings.quote: by [[INS: contemporaneous]] written records [[DEL: or other reasonable evidence]]
findings.why: Requiring contemporaneous written records is a stricter variant of the accepted 'written records' evidence standard, with the 'other reasonable evidence' option removed, which narrows the carve-outs.
findings.draft_redline: by written records or other reasonable evidence:

findings.quote: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.why: The independent development carve-out is deleted, so only three of the four required carve-outs remain.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.3 is lawfully received ... from an independent third party ... ; or 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: The independent development exception is a standard protection for both parties and we need to keep it. We have reinstated it.

findings.quote: auditors [[INS: , financing providers, private equity sponsors]] and insurers
findings.why: Adding financing providers and private equity sponsors to Representatives lets confidential information go to investors and funders, a category the playbook does not cover.
findings.draft_redline: Representatives means, in relation to a Party, the employees, officers, directors, professional advisers, auditors and insurers of that Party and of any member of its Group.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to extend permitted recipients to financing providers or private equity sponsors without separate consent. We are happy to consider disclosure to named parties case by case.

findings.quote: to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know such Confidential Information in order to evaluate or further the Purpose
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives and Group members is on a need-to-know basis and the Receiving Party is liable for them.

findings.quote: Before making any disclosure pursuant to Clause 5.1, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, with notice and cooperation only where legally permitted and resistance at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within [[DEL: ten]] [[INS: fifteen]] Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: The return period is lengthened from ten to fifteen Business Days, which is above the five Business Day minimum.
findings.fallback_cited: Any period of 5 Business Days or more.

findings.quote: copies of any Confidential Information that are securely stored in routine, automated electronic backup or archiving systems which are not readily accessible in the ordinary course of business
findings.why: Clause 6.2 already permits retention in automated backups and legally required copies, which stay confidential under 6.3; the comment asks to extend this to collaboration and messaging archives.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information, and all intellectual property rights in or relating to it, shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party
findings.why: IP stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence is granted other than use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "as is" basis.
findings.why: Information is as is, no warranty, no reliance liability except fraud, and no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement, press release or other public disclosure
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction requiring prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details and any other sharing needs a separate DPA or data sharing agreement first.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Term is two years with 30 days' notice to terminate early, as preferred.

findings.quote: shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: Survival is 3 years with Trade Secrets protected while they remain so, as preferred; the margin comment asks for 2 years from the date of disclosure, which could fall below 2 years after termination and should be escalated.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual right to seek equitable relief, with cumulative remedies in 11.2.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party shall pay to the Disclosing Party on demand the sum of £50,000 as a genuine pre-estimate of the minimum immediate administrative and investigative loss
findings.why: The insertion creates a fixed per-breach payment of 50,000 pounds, which is a liquidated sum.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the inserted sentence beginning 'Without prejudice to the foregoing' in clause 11.1.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not agree to fixed sums payable on breach; the injunctive relief and the right to claim damages at law already provide a remedy for both parties. We have removed this sentence.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure of any software, prototypes or other tangible objects
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, mortgage, charge, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner with any or all of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: Mutual restriction on assignment without prior written consent.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: English law and exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
